title: fix(plugin-auth): an IPv6 CIDR in the allowed IP ranges admits the IPv6 clients inside it, at the sign-in gate and the save check
body:

_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wgDpDyoNB672KbyavvfQQJzv)_

domain:server#2 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CXwcgsAkqebfzjnfiS

Fixes #30320

Clause-②: no — a fix: an IPv6 CIDR entry now admits the clients the list already names; no export, no new refusal, no settings key or manifest shape changes.
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：「允许的 IP 段」里的 IPv6 网段（如 `2001:db8::/32`）现在按网段生效：登录闸门放行网段内的 IPv6 用户，设置页保存时也认得出保存者的 IPv6 地址在网段内。精确的 IPv6 地址不论大小写或缩写写法都能匹配。
- 为什么改：设置说明写的是「CIDR 网段」，但匹配只认 IPv4 网段，IPv6 网段被当成一串文字比对，永远匹配不上；结果是网段里的 IPv6 用户全部登录被拒，IPv6 管理员保存这份列表也被拒。
- 风险与回滚：只放宽，不收紧。IPv4 条目的读法一字未改；IPv4 网段不会放行 IPv6 地址，IPv6 网段也不会放行 IPv4 地址；写错的 IPv6 前缀只匹配它的基地址，和以前一样不会放大。两道门共用同一个匹配函数，判法一致。回滚即撤本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` 的 `ipMatchesRange` 与 `readMatchedAddress`（地址族判定与前缀比较）；`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts` 末尾的 `#30320` 用例（经真实设置路由保存和登录闸门两道门）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts`，预期 1 个文件、11 条全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

**The rule: an allowed-IP entry is read as the address or range it names, in its own family, at every door that judges the list.**

- **`ipMatchesRange` reads IPv6 CIDR (`@objectstack/plugin-auth`).** It read IPv4 CIDR and exact addresses only; an IPv6 entry such as `2001:db8::/32` fell to an exact text comparison against its base and never matched a real client. Both sides are now read as the address they denote (`readMatchedAddress`): an IPv4 address as a uint32, any other IPv6 address as eight 16-bit groups through the file's existing `parseIpv6Literal` (`::` elision, embedded IPv4 tail). An IPv6 range compares the first `n` of 128 bits. The sign-in gate (`AuthManager.isClientIpAllowed`) and the settings save check (`allowed-ip-ranges.ts`, from #30309) both call it, so they keep judging the same address the same way.
- **Exact IPv6 entries compare by value.** `2001:DB8:0:0::1` matches `2001:db8::1`; `0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1` matches `::1`.
- **IPv4-mapped addresses stay IPv4.** A mapped address on either side, dotted (`::ffff:203.0.113.5`, as before) or hex (`::ffff:cb00:7105`, now too), is the IPv4 address it maps, so a dual-stack listener's IPv4 peers keep matching IPv4 ranges.
- **Families never cross.** An IPv4 range never admits a pure IPv6 address (`0.0.0.0/0` does not admit `::1`), and an IPv6 range never admits an IPv4 one (`::/0` does not admit `203.0.113.5` nor its mapped form).
- **Zone identifiers are dropped.** `fe80::1%eth0` is judged as `fe80::1`.
- **Malformed entries do not widen.** An IPv6 prefix must be a whole number from 0 to 128; any other prefix (`/129`, an empty `/`, `/3x`) leaves the entry matching only its base address, which is what the old exact-text fallback did. An entry that is not an address is still compared as text, which an address the server established never equals. **IPv4 entries are read exactly as before**, prefix parsing included, so no IPv4 list changes what it admits.
- `unmapIpv4` is gone (its job moved into `readMatchedAddress`; no other caller). The `isClientIpAllowed` docblock and one sentence of the `client-address-canonical.ts` header, which said the allow-list compares exact IPv6 entries as text, are corrected.
- Not changed: the `allowed_ip_ranges` help text (it promises CIDR ranges unqualified, which now holds for both families), `auth-plugin.ts`, `packages/spec`.

## Why

#30320: the setting promises CIDR ranges, and an IPv6 range locked out every IPv6 client inside it at sign-in and, after #30309, refused the save for an administrator connected from inside it, with copy saying the list does not include an address it textually covers.

## Verification

Measured first, at `d1d90b70` with the new pins: 6 failed | 7 passed (the two door pins, the CIDR pin, the exact-spelling pin, the cross-family pin through the hex-mapped case, and `isClientIpAllowed`); the malformed-prefix pin passed already, which is the preservation it states.

<details><summary>Tests</summary>

- `auth-manager.test.ts` › IP allow-list (ADR-0069 D5): five new cases — IPv6 CIDR inside/outside (`/32`, `/56`, `/128`, `::/0`, `::1`, a zone id); exact IPv6 by value; cross-family (IPv4 range vs `::1` and `2001:db8::5`, IPv6 range vs IPv4 and mapped IPv4, hex-mapped vs an IPv4 range, mapped base keeps its IPv4 prefix); malformed IPv6 prefixes never widen past the base; `isClientIpAllowed` with an IPv6 range plus `::1`.
- `allowed-ip-ranges.pin.test.ts` › `#30320` (the shared harness: real `AuthPlugin`, real `SettingsService` with the shipped auth manifest, real settings routes): the gate admits an IPv6 client inside an allowed IPv6 range and refuses one outside and an IPv4 one; a save from an IPv6 address outside is refused (`400 SETTINGS_VALIDATION`, `constraint.clientAddress`) and stores nothing, from inside is stored and enforced.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth test`: Test Files 222 passed (222), Tests 3925 passed | 10 skipped (3935), at `d9855b3c` and again at `aa57f6dd`. `typecheck`: exit 0.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- Node's `net.BlockList` was measured and not used: checked against an IPv4 subnet it admits the mapped IPv6 form, and checked as IPv4 against a `::ffff:0:0/96` subnet it admits a plain IPv4 address, so its family rules are not this matcher's; the file already carries an IPv6 parser.
- A zone identifier is dropped on both sides rather than refused: no save-time refusal is added here.
